paragraphs: Polaris Inc., formerly known as Polaris Industries Inc., a Delaware corporation, was formed in 1994 and is the successor to Polaris Industries Partners LP. The terms "Polaris," the "Company," "we," "us," and "our" as used herein refer to the business and operations of Polaris Inc., its subsidiaries and its predecessors, which began doing business in 1954. We design, engineer, manufacture and market powersports vehicles which include: off-road vehicles ("ORV"), including all-terrain vehicles ("ATV") and side-by-side vehicles; military and commercial ORVs; snowmobiles; moto-roadsters; quadricycles; and boats. We also design and manufacture or source parts, garments and accessories ("PG&A"), which includes aftermarket accessories and apparel. Our products are sold online and through dealers and distributors principally located in the United States, Canada, Western Europe, Australia, and Mexico.

We operate in three business segments; Off Road, On Road, and Marine. Our products are sold through a network of approximately 2,400 independent dealers in North America. Internationally, products are sold through 25 subsidiaries to over 1,500 independent international dealers and 70 independent distributors that serve over 90 countries outside of North America. A majority of our dealers and distributors are multi-line and also carry competitor products; however, some dealers carry our full line of products and, while relatively consistent, the actual number of dealers carrying our products can vary from time to time.

The Off Road segment primarily consists of ORVs and snowmobiles. ORVs are four-wheel vehicles designed for off-road use and traversing a wide variety of terrain, including dunes, trails, and mud. The vehicles can be multi-passenger or single passenger, are used for recreation in sports such as fishing and hunting and for trail and dune riding, and for utility purposes on farms, ranches, and construction sites. The ORV industry is comprised of ATVs and side-by-side vehicles. Internationally, ATVs and side-by-sides are sold primarily in Western Europe, Australia, and Mexico by similar manufacturers as in North America.

*Estimates are unaudited and based on internally-generated management estimates, including estimates based on extrapolations from third-party surveys of the industries in which we compete. See Market and Industry Data section for additional information.

The side-by-side market has been consistently strong over the past several years primarily due to continued innovation by manufacturers. In 2025, we continued to be the North America market share leader in off-road vehicles. Our ORV lineup includes the RZR sport side-by-side, the RANGER utility side-by-side, the GENERAL crossover side-by-side, the Polaris XPEDITION adventure side-by-side and the Sportsman ATV. The full line spans 90 models, including two-, four- and six-wheel drive general purpose and recreational vehicles. In many of our segments, we offer youth, value, mid-size, premium and extreme-performance vehicles, which come in both single passenger and multi-passenger seating arrangements. Key 2025 ORV product introductions and upgrades included the RANGER 500 mid-size utility vehicle, a new value offering, as well as updates within the RANGER XD 1500, including two new trim levels, Mountaineer and Texas Edition. In the RZR portfolio, we introduced a redesigned RZR XP and a new 72-inch wide RZR XP S. In addition, we added the largest screen on the market, a 10.4-inch touchscreen, to our popular RZR Pro R models.

We sell our ORVs directly to a network of approximately 1,300 dealers in North America and 1,000 international dealers. Many of our ORV dealers and distributors are also authorized snowmobile dealers. We produce and deliver our

products throughout the year based on dealer, distributor, and customer orders. ORV retail sales activity at the dealer level drives orders that are incorporated into each product's production scheduling. International distributor ORV orders are taken throughout the year. We utilize our Retail Flow Management ("RFM") ordering system for ORV dealers, which allows dealers to order daily and create a segment stocking order which helps to reduce order fulfillment times.

The ORV industry in the United States, Canada and other global markets is highly competitive. As an ORV original equipment manufacturer ("OEM"), our competition primarily comes from North American and Asian manufacturers. Competition in such markets is based upon a number of factors, including price, quality, reliability, styling, product features, warranties and a manufacturer's ability to produce vehicles to meet changing consumer demand.

Snowmobiles have been manufactured under the Polaris name since 1954. We estimate that worldwide industry sales of snowmobiles totaled approximately 90,000, 110,000, and 125,000 units for the 12 month seasons ended March 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.

For the 12 month snowmobile season ended March 31, 2025, we held the number two market share position for North America. We produce a full line of snowmobiles consisting of 68 models, ranging from entry models to utility and economy models to performance and competition models.

headings: Our business may be sensitive to economic conditions, including those that impact our customers' spending.
Shortages or increases in the cost of raw materials, commodities, component parts, and transportation could negatively impact our business.
Our business may be adversely affected by trade matters, including tariffs.
We face intense competition in all product lines. Failure to compete effectively against competitors could negatively impact our business and operating results.
Our continued success is dependent on positive perceptions of our Polaris brands which, if weakened, could adversely affect our sales.

From time to time, we manage our portfolio through acquisitions, non-consolidated investments, alliances, new joint ventures and partnerships, and divestitures, which could be risky and could harm our business.
Disruption in our suppliers' operations could disrupt our production schedule.

We depend on suppliers, financing sources and other strategic partners who may be sensitive to economic conditions that could affect their businesses in a manner that adversely affects their relationship with us.
Weather conditions may reduce demand and negatively impact net sales and production of certain of our products.
A significant adverse determination in any material litigation claim against us could adversely affect our operating results or financial condition.
Significant product repair and/or replacement costs due to product warranty claims or product recalls could have a material adverse impact on our results of operations.
Regulatory, Intellectual Property, Cybersecurity and Privacy Risks
We may be subject to cybersecurity events and other disruptions to our information technology systems, data and products that could adversely affect our business.
Fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates could result in declines in our reported sales and net earnings.
Retail credit market deterioration and volatility may restrict the ability of our retail customers to finance the purchase of our products.
Additional tax expense or tax exposure could impact our financial performance.
An impairment in the carrying value of goodwill and trade names could negatively impact our consolidated results of operations and net worth.
Expectations relating to environmental, social and governance considerations expose us to potential liabilities, increased costs, reputational harm and other adverse effects on our business.
paragraphs: The following are factors known to us that could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, cash flows, or operating results, as well as adversely affect the value of an investment in our common stock.

Our results of operations have been, and may continue to be sensitive to changes in overall economic conditions, primarily in North America and Europe, that impact spending on our products, including discretionary spending. Weakening of, and fluctuations in, general economic conditions affecting the disposable income and budgets of our customers, such as employment levels, inflation, business conditions, the level of governmental financial assistance, the impacts of changing government regulation and tariffs, changes in housing market conditions, capital markets, tax rates, savings rates, interest rates, fuel and energy costs, the economic impacts of natural disasters or other severe weather conditions, acts of war, acts of terrorism, and the availability of consumer credit, could reduce overall spending or reduce spending on our products. Our sales growth and profitability have been from time to time, and in the future could be, affected by a general reduction in consumer spending or a reduction in consumer spending on powersports, boats and aftermarket products in particular. A general reduction in spending by our customers for commercial equipment or a reduction in government budgets or actual spending could adversely affect our related sales.

Adverse changes in these factors has previously, and may in the future, lead to a decreased level of demand for our products, which could negatively impact our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

In addition, we have current and prior financial services arrangements with subsidiaries of Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and a subsidiary of Huntington Bancshares Incorporated that require us to repurchase products financed and repossessed pursuant to the terms of such arrangements and subject to certain limitations. From time to time, we may also elect to

provide guarantees or other credit support in favor of, or related to, these arrangements, including to increase capacity thereunder. If adverse changes to economic conditions result in increased defaults on the loans made under these arrangements, our contractual repurchase obligations (or demands under any guarantees or other credit support) could adversely affect our liquidity and harm our business.

The primary commodities used in manufacturing our products are aluminum, steel, copper, petroleum-based resins and certain rare earth metals, as well as diesel fuel to transport products. Our profitability has been affected by fluctuations in the prices of the raw materials and commodities we use in our products and in the cost of freight and shipping to source materials, commodities, and other component parts necessary to assemble our products. In the past, we have experienced significant increases in the cost of these commodities and materials due generally to an inflationary environment driven by high demand and supply chain disruptions. All of these could adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

paragraphs: The following discussion pertains to the results of operations and financial position of the Company and should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and the Notes thereto included elsewhere in this Annual Report. This section of this Annual Report generally discusses 2025 and 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2025 and 2024. Discussions of 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2024 and 2023 that are not included in this Annual Report can be found in "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024.

2025 sales totaled $7.2 billion and were approximately flat as compared to 2024. This was primarily driven by decreased shipments and lower net pricing driven by higher promotional costs, mostly offset by product mix.

Our gross profit of $1.4 billion decreased seven percent from $1.5 billion in 2024. Gross profit, as a percentage of sales, decreased primarily due to incremental tariff charges, lower net pricing driven by higher promotional costs and increased incentive compensation costs, partially offset by favorable operational costs and reduced warranty expense.

Full year net loss attributable to Polaris Inc. was $465.5 million, or $8.18 net loss per diluted share, compared to 2024 full year net income attributable to Polaris Inc. of $110.8 million, or $1.95 per diluted share. These decreases were primarily the result of impairment and other charges recorded as a result of the Indian Motorcycle business being classified as held for sale, goodwill and other intangible asset impairment charges recorded, incremental tariff charges and increased incentive compensation costs, partially offset by favorable operating costs. We reported Adjusted EBITDA of $410.2 million in 2025 compared to $635.4 million in 2024. For information on how we define and calculate Adjusted EBITDA, and a reconciliation from net (loss) income to Adjusted EBITDA, see "Non-GAAP Financial Measures".

On October 10, 2025, we entered into a definitive agreement to sell a majority interest in the Indian Motorcycle business. During the year ended December 31, 2025, operating results of the Indian Motorcycle business were reported in our On Road segment and its assets and liabilities were classified as held for sale as of December 31, 2025. The sale closed in the first quarter of 2026.

On January 29, 2026, we announced that our Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.68 per share for the first quarter of 2026, a one percent increase from the prior quarterly cash dividend, representing the 31st consecutive year of increased dividends to shareholders.

We continue to monitor macroeconomic trends and uncertainties and changes in international trade relations and trade policy, including those related to tariffs. The U.S. government has implemented a general tariff on all imports from countries not exempted under certain trade reciprocity criteria and elevated tariffs have been imposed on imports from major trading partners. Impacted countries have and may impose retaliatory tariffs, and such actions could give rise to an escalation of other trade measures by the countries subjected to such tariffs. Although the validity of certain tariffs are being challenged in litigation pending before the Supreme Court of the United States, there can be no guarantee about the outcome of such proceedings. The tariff policy environment is rapidly evolving and there is no guarantee that additional or increased tariffs will not be imposed.

We currently procure components from countries subject to such tariffs, which are utilized in our facilities in the United States and Mexico. A portion of our annual sales originate from products manufactured in our facilities in Mexico, and we sell our products globally. As a result of the current tariffs, we anticipate increased supply chain challenges, commodity cost volatility, economic uncertainty, and economic pressures on customers and consumers as a result of the challenges of high inflation combined with the effects of increased tariffs. To mitigate the impact of tariffs on our supply chain and manufacturing, we continue to evaluate sourcing alternatives, negotiate with suppliers, and work to increase the percentage of shipments qualified under favorable trade agreements. Incremental tariffs and changed trade policies had a notable impact on our financial results for 2025, and could continue to adversely impact our results in the future. We will continue to evaluate the impact of tariffs on our operations and profitability.

paragraphs: Polaris Inc., 以前稱為 Polaris Industries Inc., 為一間 Delaware 公司，於 1994 年成立，為 Polaris Industries Partners LP 的繼承者。本文所用之 "Polaris"、"本公司"、"我們"、"我們"及 "我們的" 皆指 Polaris Inc.、其子公司及前身之業務與運作，其業務於 1954 年開始。我們設計、工程、製造與行銷 powersports 車輛，包括：越野車輛（"ORV"），包括全地形車輛（"ATV"）及側邊對側車輛；軍事與商業 ORV；雪地摩托；摩托路車；四輪車；以及船隻。我們也設計與製造或來源零組件、服飾與配件（"PG&A"），包括後市場配件與服飾。我們的產品透過線上與經銷商與代理商銷售，主要位於美國、加拿大、西歐、澳洲與墨西哥。

我們經營三個業務分部；Off Road、On Road 與 Marine。我們的產品透過約 2,400 家獨立經銷商銷售於北美地區。國際上，產品透過 25 家子公司銷售至超過 1,500 家獨立國際經銷商與 70 家獨立代理商，服務超過 90 個國家地區。我們的大多數經銷商與代理商為多線經營，同時銷售競爭對手產品；然而，有些經銷商銷售我們全系列產品，雖然相對穩定，但實際銷售我們產品的經銷商數量可能隨時間而有所變動。
Off Road 分部主要由 ORV 與雪地摩托組成。ORV 為四輪車輛，設計用於越野用途，可穿越多種地形，包括沙丘、小徑與泥地。這些車輛可為多人乘坐或單人乘坐，用於釣魚與狩獵等運動娛樂，以及農場、牧場與建設工地的實用用途。ORV 行業由 ATV 與側邊對側車輛組成。國際上，ATV 與側邊對側車輛主要在西歐、澳洲與墨西哥由與北美地區相似的製造商銷售。
預估北美與全球 ORV 行業零售銷售額總結如下：
*估計為未審計，基於內部產生的管理估計，包括基於第三方調查的產業競爭行業的外推估計。請參閱市場與產業資料部分以取得更多資訊。

側邊馬達車市場在過去幾年一直表現強勁，主要歸因於製造商持續的創新。2025年，我們繼續在北美市場的越野車（ORV）市場佔有率位居第一。我們的ORV產品線包括RZR sport側邊馬達車、RANGER實用側邊馬達車、GENERAL跨界側邊馬達車、Polaris XPEDITION冒險側邊馬達車以及Sportsman ATV。完整的產品線涵蓋90種型號，包括二輪、四輪和六輪驅動的通用與休閒用車。在許多我們的產品線中，我們提供兒童、經濟型、中型、豪華與極致性能車款，這些車款提供單人與多人座的座位配置。2025年重要的ORV產品推出與升級包括RANGER 500中型實用車款，這是一款新的經濟型產品，以及RANGER XD 1500的更新，包括兩種新的車型等級，Mountaineer與Texas Edition。在RZR產品線中，我們推出重新設計的RZR XP與一款72英寸寬的RZR XP S。此外，我們在熱門的RZR Pro R車型中加入了市場上最大的螢幕，10.4英寸觸控螢幕。

我們直接將ORV銷售給約1,300家北美經銷商與1,000家國際經銷商。許多我們的ORV經銷商與分銷商同時也是授權的雪地摩托經銷商。我們根據經銷商、分銷商與客戶的訂單全年生產與交付產品。ORV零售銷售活動在經銷商層面驅動訂單，這些訂單被納入每款產品的生產排程中。國際分銷商的ORV訂單全年皆可接單。我們使用零售流管理（"Retail Flow Management"，簡稱RFM）訂購系統為ORV經銷商，這讓經銷商可以每日訂購並建立分區庫存訂單，有助於減少訂單履行時間。
我們根據經銷商、分銷商與客戶的訂單全年生產與交付產品。ORV零售銷售活動在經銷商層面驅動訂單，這些訂單被納入每款產品的生產排程中。國際分銷商的ORV訂單全年皆可接單。我們使用零售流管理（"Retail Flow Management"，簡稱RFM）訂購系統為ORV經銷商，這讓經銷商可以每日訂購並建立分區庫存訂單，有助於減少訂單履行時間。
美國、加拿大及其他全球市場的ORV產業競爭激烈。作為ORV原廠製造商（"OEM"），我們的主要競爭對手來自北美與亞洲製造商。這些市場的競爭基於多種因素，包括價格、品質、可靠性、外觀設計、產品功能、保固以及製造商滿足變動消費者需求的生產能力。
雪地摩托自1954年起便以Polaris為品牌製造。我們估計，全球雪地摩托銷售量在截至2025年3月31日的12個月季節分別為約90,000臺、110,000臺與125,000臺。
截至2025年3月31日的12個月雪地摩托銷售季節中，我們在北美市場的市場佔有率為第二名。我們生產完整的雪地摩托產品線，包含68種型號，從入門型到實用與經濟型，再到性能與競賽型。

paragraphs: 以下討論內容涉及本公司營運成果與財務狀況，應與本年度財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。本年度財務報告此部分一般討論 2025 年與 2024 年項目及 2025 年與 2024 年的年對年比較。未包含於本年度財務報告中的 2023 年項目及 2024 年與 2023 年的年對年比較，可參閱我們 2024 年 12 月 31 日財務年度 10-K 表報表中第二部分，第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」。
2025 年銷售額為 7.2 十億美元，與 2024 年相比大致持平。這主要是由於出貨量減少及淨售價下降，因促銷成本增加所致，但因產品組成有所改善而部分抵銷。
我們的毛利為 1.4 十億美元，較 2024 年的 1.5 十億美元減少 7%。毛利佔銷售額的百分比下降，主要是由於額外關稅費用、因促銷成本增加導致的淨售價下降以及增加的激勵薪資費用，部分因有利的營運費用及減少的保固費用而抵銷。

全年淨損歸屬於 Polaris Inc. 為 465.5 百萬美元，或每股稀釋普通股淨損 8.18 美元，與 2024 年全年淨收入歸屬於 Polaris Inc. 的 110.8 百萬美元，或每股稀釋普通股淨收入 1.95 美元相比。此減少主要係因印度摩托車業務被歸類為持有待售，因而記入減損及其它費用，以及記入 goodwill 及其它無形資產減損費用，以及增加的關稅費用及激勵薪酬費用，部分抵銷有利的營運費用。我們在 2025 年報告的調整後營運資金為 410.2 百萬美元，與 2024 年的 635.4 百萬美元相比。有關我們如何定義及計算調整後營運資金，以及從淨（損）收入到調整後營運資金的調整，請參閱 "Non-GAAP 財務指標"。
2025 年 10 月 10 日，我們與買方簽訂了買賣印度摩托車業務多數股權的最終協議。在 2025 年 12 月 31 日結業年度內，印度摩托車業務的營運成果被歸入我們的 On Road 分部，其資產與負債於 2025 年 12 月 31 日被歸類為待售。交易於 2026 年第一季完成。
2026 年 1 月 29 日，我們宣佈，董事會已宣佈 2026 年第一季每股 0.68 美元的季度現金股息，較前一季的季度現金股息增加 1%，這是連續第 31 年提高對股東的股息。

我們持續監測總體經濟趨勢與不確定性，以及國際貿易關係與貿易政策的變化，包括與關稅相關的內容。美國政府已對未符合特定貿易互惠標準豁免的國家所有進口商品課徵一般關稅，並對主要貿易夥伴的進口商品課徵提高的關稅。受影響的國家已並可能對美國課徵報復性關稅，這些行動可能導致這些國家對美國課徵關稅的國家採取其他貿易措施。雖然某些關稅的合法性正在美國最高法院進行訴訟，但無法保證這些訴訟的結果。關稅政策環境正在快速變化，無法保證不會增加或提高關稅。

我們目前從課徵關稅的國家進口零組件，這些零組件用於我們美國與墨西哥的工廠。我們年度銷售的一部分來自於墨西哥工廠製造的產品，我們將產品銷售至全球各地。由於現行關稅，我們預期將面臨供應鏈挑戰增加、原材料成本波動、經濟不確定性，以及因高通貨膨脹與關稅增加所導致的客戶與消費者經濟壓力。為緩解關稅對我們供應鏈與製造的影響，我們持續評估來源選項、與供應商協商，並努力提高符合有利貿易協議的出貨比例。額外關稅與貿易政策的變動對我們 2025 年的財務結果有顯著影響，並可能繼續對我們未來的結果產生不利影響。我們將持續評估關稅對我們營運與獲利的影響。

headings: 本公司業務可能受到經濟狀況的影響，包括影響客戶支出的情況。
原材料、商品、零組件及運輸成本的短缺或增加，可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
本公司業務可能因貿易相關事項，包括關稅，而受到不利影響。
我們在所有產品線均面臨激烈競爭。若無法有效競爭，可能對本公司業務及營運成果產生負面影響。
本公司持續成功取決於客戶對 Polaris 品牌的正面看法，若該看法受到削弱，可能對本公司銷售產生不利影響。
有時，本公司會透過收購、未合併投資、聯盟、新合資企業及合作夥伴關係，以及資產處置來管理投資組合，這些行動可能具有風險，並可能對本公司業務造成損害。
我們供應商的營運中斷可能幹擾我們的生產排程。
我們依賴供應商、資金來源及其他戰略夥伴，這些夥伴可能對總體經濟條件敏感，而這些條件可能影響他們的業務，進而對他們與我們的關係產生不利影響。
天氣條件可能降低需求，並對我們某些產品的淨銷售額及生產造成負面影響。
任何重大不利的裁決，針對我們的重大訴訟聲請，可能對我們的營運成果或財務狀況產生不利影響。
因產品保固聲請或產品回收而產生的重大產品維修及/或更換成本，可能對我們的營運成果產生重大不利影響。
法規、智慧財產權、網路安全及隱私權風險
我們可能面臨網路安全事件及其他資訊科技系統、資料與產品的中斷，這可能會對我們的業務產生不利影響。
外幣交換率波動可能會導致我們報告的銷售額與淨獲利下降。
零售信貸市場的惡化與波動可能限制我們零售客戶購買我們產品的融資能力。
額外的稅務費用或稅務風險可能會影響我們的財務表現。
商譽與商標的攜帶價值減損可能會對我們的合併營運成果與淨資產產生負面影響。
與環境、社會及治理考量相關的預期，可能會使我們面臨潛在負債、成本增加、聲譽損害及其他對我們業務的不利影響。
paragraphs: 下列為本公司所知，可能重大不利影響本公司業務、財務狀況、現金流或營運成果，以及不利影響投資本公司普通股價值之因素。

本公司營運成果已受到，且可能持續受到總體經濟條件變動之影響，主要為北美及歐洲地區，此等條件影響客戶對本公司產品之支出，包括非必要性支出。總體經濟條件之減弱及波動，影響本公司客戶之可支配所得與預算，例如就業水平、通貨膨脹、營商條件、政府財政援助程度、政府規範與關稅變動、住宅市場條件、資本市場、稅率、儲蓄率、利率、燃料與能源成本、天然災害或其他嚴峻天氣條件之經濟影響、戰爭行為、恐怖攻擊行為，以及消費者信貸之可取得性，可能減少總體支出或減少對本公司產品之支出。本公司銷售成長與獲利有時已受到，且未來可能再次受到消費者支出減少或特別針對休閒運動器材、船隻與後市場產品之消費者支出減少之影響。本公司客戶對商業設備之支出減少，或政府預算或實際支出減少，可能對本公司相關銷售造成不利影響。
這些因素之不利變動已於過往，且可能於未來導致本公司產品之需求程度降低，此可能對本公司業務、營運成果、財務狀況與現金流造成負面影響。
此外，本公司與華盛頓銀行（Wells Fargo Bank, N.A.）之子公司及漢密爾頓銀行持股公司（Huntington Bancshares Incorporated）之子公司現有及過去之金融服務協議，要求本公司於符合特定限制條件下，購回依該等協議條款所融資並被收回之產品。有時，本公司亦可能選擇
提供擔保或其他信用支援，以支持或與這些協議相關，包括以增加其信用額度。若總體經濟條件之不利變動導致這些協議下貸款之違約率增加，本公司之契約購回義務（或擔保或其他信用支援下之索償要求）可能對本公司流動性造成不利影響，並損害本公司業務。
本公司製造產品所使用之主要原材料為鋁、鋼、銅、石油基樹脂及某些稀有金屬，以及柴油用以運輸產品。本公司獲利已受到所使用原材料與商品價格波動，以及取得原材料、商品及其他組裝產品所需零組件之運輸與物流成本之影響。過往，本公司因通貨膨脹環境所導致之高需求與供應鏈中斷，已經驗到這些原材料與商品成本顯著上升。所有這些因素均可能對本公司營運成果與財務狀況造成不利影響。
